# Data-quality record (numbers generated by training/run_eda.py)

Trips analysed: 90 (student_test: 10, train: 80).
Unique road networks: 90 (identical `.nodes` + `.arcs` files across trips share one network).

| Check | Trips affected |
|---|---|
| non-finite GPS values | 0 |
| duplicate GPS rows | 0 |
| timestamps not strictly increasing | 0 |
| gap > 5 s between observations | 47 |
| coordinates out of range | 0 |
| GPS outside network bounding box | 0 |
| no reference route file | 0 |
| reference route has breaks | 11 |
| network has isolated nodes | 0 |
| network not weakly connected | 89 |
| arcs referencing invalid nodes | 0 |

## Key measurements
- Sampling: median interval 1.0 s; 94.3% of steps are exactly 1 s; largest gap anywhere 153064 s.
- Trajectory length 5.5-169.3 km; observations per trip 262-19313.
- Speed: mean of trip means 55 km/h; largest single-step speed 649 km/h.
- Local equirectangular projection vs haversine: worst per-step error 0.777%, worst start-to-end error 0.162%.
- Reference route (trips with route: 90): GPS-to-route distance median 5.6 m, 95th percentile 137.7 m, max 569.5 m.
- Network size per trip: 299-155003 nodes, 649-307392 arcs.

## Assumptions and decisions (review and edit before submitting)
- Column order is lon, lat, t for `.track` and lon, lat for `.nodes`, as documented; extents above are plausible for one region.
- Distances are computed in local metres (equirectangular projection centred on each trip); degrees are never used as distances.
- The reference route is treated as reference information, not error-free ground truth: GPS points do not lie exactly on it.
- A GPS row does not correspond to a road-network row; the link between them is built later by candidate generation.
- Partitions are never mixed: each trip belongs to exactly one partition.
